entries.task_id: based|creoles|worldwide with the highest number of speakers
entries.description: based creoles worldwide with the highest number of speakers
entries.subject: based
entries.object: worldwide with the highest number of speakers

spans.text: Alongside Papiamentu and Palenquero in the Americas, Chabacano, with its variety Zamboangueño, is one of three Spanish-based creoles worldwide with the highest number of speakers.

entries.task_id: based|creoles|in asia
entries.description: based creoles in Asia
entries.subject: based

spans.text: It shares interesting features with other European-based creoles in Asia, a fact that distinguishes it from the Atlantic creoles.
For a comparison of all varieties of Chabacano and a comparison of these with Portuguese-based creoles in Asia, see Steinkrüger (2013+).

entries.task_id: zamboanga chabacano|has|been acquiring a mixed character
entries.description: Zamboanga Chabacano has been acquiring a mixed character
entries.subject: Zamboanga Chabacano

spans.text: Furthermore, unlike these, Zamboanga Chabacano has been acquiring a mixed character, especially from the 20th century onwards.

entries.task_id: zamboanga chabacano|is|also named southern mindanao creole
entries.description: Zamboanga Chabacano is also named Southern Mindanao Creole
entries.subject: Zamboanga Chabacano

spans.text: In scientific publications, Zamboanga Chabacano is also named Southern Mindanao Creole.
Zamboanga Chabacano is spoken on the island Mindanao in the south of the archipelago.

entries.task_id: manila bay|creoles|(cavite and ternate chabacano)
entries.description: Manila Bay creoles (Cavite and Ternate Chabacano)
entries.subject: Manila Bay

spans.text: Whinnom considered Zamboanga Chabacano a layer of the Manila Bay creoles (Cavite and Ternate Chabacano).

entries.task_id: language pilipino|increased|and especially affected the lexicon
entries.description: language Pilipino increased and especially affected the lexicon
entries.subject: language Pilipino

spans.text: From the 1930s onwards, the influence of English and, after the Second World War, that of the national language Pilipino (= Tagalog) increased and especially affected the lexicon.

entries.task_id:
and
endogenous|creoles|adequately describe the situation of zamboanga chabacano
entries.description:
and
endogenous creoles adequately describe the situation of Zamboanga Chabacano
entries.subject:
and
endogenous
entries.object: adequately describe the situation of Zamboanga Chabacano

spans.text: Consequently, Zamboanga Chabacano does not fit into the classification of plantation, fort, and maritime creoles, nor can the dichotomy of exogenous and endogenous creoles adequately describe the situation of Zamboanga Chabacano, but it can probably be classified as a complex mixture of maritime, fort, and maroon creole.

entries.task_id: zamboanga city|has|a total population of 600
entries.description: Zamboanga City has a total population of 600
entries.subject: Zamboanga City

spans.text: Zamboanga City has a total population of 600,000 inhabitants (official census 2000).

entries.task_id: the population|are|christians
entries.description: the population are Christians
entries.subject: the population

spans.text: Approximately two thirds of the population are Christians, mostly Catholics, and the remaining part are Muslims.

entries.task_id: remaining part|are|muslims
entries.description: remaining part are Muslims
entries.subject: remaining part

spans.text: Approximately two thirds of the population are Christians, mostly Catholics, and the remaining part are Muslims.

entries.task_id: in zamboanga|are|cebuano
entries.description: in Zamboanga are Cebuano
entries.subject: in Zamboanga

spans.text: Besides Chabacano, the main languages in Zamboanga are Cebuano, Tagalog, and Hokkien Chinese.

entries.task_id: zamboanga chabacano|is|the dominant language of about half of the population
entries.description: Zamboanga Chabacano is the dominant language of about half of the population
entries.subject: Zamboanga Chabacano
entries.object: the dominant language of about half of the population

spans.text: Zamboanga Chabacano is the dominant language of about half of the population; it is decreasing as such but expanding as a second language, even in wider areas of the Sulu and Celebes Seas.

entries.task_id: it|is|decreasing as such but expanding as a second language
entries.description: it is decreasing as such but expanding as a second language
entries.subject: it
entries.object: decreasing as such but expanding as a second language

spans.text: Zamboanga Chabacano is the dominant language of about half of the population; it is decreasing as such but expanding as a second language, even in wider areas of the Sulu and Celebes Seas.

entries.task_id: zamboanga chabacano|has|five (potentially) phonemic vowels in stressed syllables
entries.description: Zamboanga Chabacano has five (potentially) phonemic vowels in stressed syllables
entries.subject: Zamboanga Chabacano
entries.object: five (potentially) phonemic vowels in stressed syllables

spans.text: Zamboanga Chabacano has five (potentially) phonemic vowels in stressed syllables, namely /e, i, a, o, u/.

entries.task_id: whether there|are|really minimal pairs contrasting /i/ vs
entries.description: whether there are really minimal pairs contrasting /i/ vs
entries.subject: whether there

spans.text: It is still open to debate whether there are really minimal pairs contrasting /i/ vs. /e/ and /u/ vs. /o/ even in stressed syllables.

entries.task_id: two phonemes|are|only potentially differentiated by the speakers (see also forman 1972: 89)
entries.description: two phonemes are only potentially differentiated by the speakers (see also Forman 1972: 89)
entries.subject: two phonemes
entries.object: only potentially differentiated by the speakers (see also Forman 1972: 89)

spans.text: Taking into consideration spelling “mistakes” such as gropo ‘group’ (< Spanish grupo) or the two variants salí and salé (both meaning ‘leave; get out’ < Spanish salir), these two phonemes are only potentially differentiated by the speakers (see also Forman 1972: 89).

entries.task_id:
and
there|are|only a few cases with phonemic contrasts
entries.description:
and
there are only a few cases with phonemic contrasts
entries.subject:
and
there
entries.object: only a few cases with phonemic contrasts

spans.text: The glottal stop is, in nearly all cases, only a boundary marker between syllables starting with a vowel, and there are only a few cases with phonemic contrasts, but these occur exclusively in words of Austronesian origin such as bátaq ‘child’ vs. báta ‘(woman’s) nightgown’.

entries.task_id: word stress|is|distinctive
entries.description: Word stress is distinctive
entries.subject: Word stress

spans.text: Word stress is distinctive; for example: nadá ‘to swim’ (< Spanish nadar) vs. náda ‘nothing’ (< Spanish nada).

entries.task_id: the noun|is|invariable
entries.description: The noun is invariable
entries.subject: The noun

spans.text: The noun is invariable.

entries.task_id: natural gender|is|usually distinguished by different words
entries.description: Natural gender is usually distinguished by different words
entries.subject: Natural gender

spans.text: Natural gender is usually distinguished by different words, as nána ‘mother’ vs. tay ‘father’, or by muhér ‘woman’ and ómbre ‘man’ following the noun, as in karabáw ómbre ‘male water buffalo’ vs. karabáw muhér ‘female water buffalo’.
